subject: general
question: Sapna invested ₹22,800 on simple interest, partly at 14% per annum and partly at 7% per annum. If she earns equal interests from the two investments after 6 years, then find the sum invested at 14% per annum (in ₹).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For equal simple interests over the same time period, principals are inversely proportional to the interest rates.

Ratio of investments P₁ : P₂ = R₂ : R₁ = 7 : 14 = 1 : 2.

Total ratio parts = 1 + 2 = 3 parts.

3 parts → ₹22,800 ⇒ 1 part → ₹7,600.

Sum invested at 14% is 1 part, which is ₹7,600.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total investment = ₹22,800

Rate for 1st part (R₁) = 14% per annum

Rate for 2nd part (R₂) = 7% per annum

Time (T) = 6 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100
